description: Advice-only response cases for combining winml perf --endpoint reports and rendering a shareable deck. Assertions are ungraded placeholders: passed null and empty evidence. Validate every concrete command against the scripts' --help.

evals.name: combine-and-render
evals.prompt: I have plain-0.json, plain-1.json, draft-0.json and draft-1.json from winml perf --endpoint (labels config=plain and config=draft). How do I turn them into slides I can share with my team?

assertions.text: Runs combine.py over the reports with --baseline config=plain and -o pointing to a combined JSON file.
Runs render_slides.py on the combined JSON with -o pointing to a .pptx file.
Uses uv run so python-pptx is installed in an isolated environment rather than added to winml-cli.
Keeps reports, the combined JSON and the deck outside the repository.
Suggests reviewing the method and provenance slide before sharing.

evals.name: slower-config
evals.prompt: my combined report says the draft config is 0.8x of plain. that can't be right, speculative decoding is supposed to be faster. can you just leave that slide out?

assertions.text: Explains that a speedup below 1.00x is a valid measured result and does not hide or alter it.
Points to the run-range check and the per-run chart to judge whether the difference exceeds run-to-run noise.
Suggests checking draft acceptance per cohort and the draft model's cost as possible causes.
Does not state speedups or acceptance rates that were not produced in the session.

evals.name: nondeterministic-outputs
evals.prompt: the deck says only 60% of outputs match between my two plain runs and 45% between draft and plain. is speculative decoding changing the answers?

assertions.text: Explains that the within-series rate of the baseline is the determinism of the setup.
Compares the vs-baseline rate with the baseline's within-series rate rather than with 100 percent.
Does not conclude identical or changed outputs from a single comparison and suggests more runs.

evals.name: mismatch-warnings
evals.prompt: combine.py printed warnings about different prompts_sha256 and max_new_tokens. can I still use the deck?

assertions.text: Explains that series are only comparable when they sent the same prompts with the same settings.
Recommends rerunning with matching settings or combining only the matching reports.
Notes that the warnings appear on the caveats slide if the deck is shared anyway.
